stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of a Nahua account in the Florentine Codex (16th century), public domain; compiled by Bernardino de Sahagun with Nahua scholars.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of a Nahua account of smallpox in Tenochtitlan, recorded in the Florentine Codex, compiled by the Franciscan friar Bernardino de Sahagun with Nahua scholars in the 1500s. The account describes the sick lying in their houses and sleeping places, no longer able to move or stir, while the healthy could not bury the dead fast enough. Whole neighborhoods fell ill at once.

stem: Within a century of sustained contact, Native populations in many parts of the Spanish colonies had collapsed catastrophically. Which broader process best explains the context of this demographic catastrophe?

options.text: The introduction of European livestock, which trampled Native fields and ruined food supplies
options.misconception: Livestock altered landscapes and diets, but they did not cause the population collapse.

options.text: Mass migration of Native peoples to French trading posts far to the north
options.misconception: There was no such mass migration; populations collapsed in place.

options.text: The spread of Old World diseases like smallpox to peoples with no immunity
The Spanish crown's official policy of extermination of Native peoples
options.misconception: The crown sought Native labor and tribute, not extermination; the catastrophe came from disease rather than policy.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
